newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - JGB volatility mired at lows before poll.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - JGB volatility mired at lows before poll.

text.p: General elections are the stuff of which exciting options trade is made but dealers said on Friday few players were showing much enthusiasm for Japanese government bond options, where volatility is languishing at low levels.
Japanese voters go to the polls on Sunday. Analysts are forecasting a comeback for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party, which was trounced in 1993.
But the options market, which thrives on political uncertainty, is relatively sanguine.
"Vol itself is still on its lows or near the lows," said a trader at a bank in Paris.
There were overnight flows in the options market, but the trader said most interest, which centered on nine and 10-year JGB options, was for downside protection.
"There's no speculation and the vol curve being a normal shape does not highlight any great panic or expectation," the trader said.
In a normal vol curve, implied volatility levels rise as the contract maturities increase, showing the premium buyers will pay for longer-dated options.
One week JGB price volatility was around 3.75 percent, rising to four percent for one-month vols, 4.2 percent for two- and three-month vols, and 4.3 percent for six-month vols.

Alex McGuire, options trader at Sumitomo Finance International in London, said vols on the benchmark No 182 JGB have been easing slightly in the past couple of days but generally have been hovering near the four percent level.
He said there was a general view in the market that the Japanese election would not spring any great surprises.
Traders said the usual pre-weekend torpor was also evident.

"Ahead of the weekend I think nobody wants to take new positions," said a dealer at a French bank in London. The only place where volatility was strong, he said, was in high-yielding markets but these were quite illiquid.
Japanese volatility levels are down about half a percentage point from three months ago and are languishing at some of their lowest levels in a year, traders said.

"All year vol has basically come off in bond markets and people continue to look to initate trades by selling vol rather than buying," the Paris trader said. But he said vol was starting to look cheap now and might represent a good buy.
The market is also taking a wait-and-see attitude to a 10-year JGB auction expected next Tuesday.

The market had been trending higher since mid-July although it has suffered a setback in the past week. Talk of a potentially expansionary budget after the elections weighed on the market earlier in the week.
December JGB futures on LIFFE at 1400 GMT were at 122.92, up from the 122.84 close Tokyo futures posted.
The No. 182 JGB was yielding 2.805 percent.
